name: Priestess (AVV)
body:
Seers, shamans, druids, oracles, judges, and shepherds are all different types of priestesses. As community leaders, messengers of the deities, and heads of the faith, priestesses play an important role in every society.

Priestesses are the custodians of lore and ancient wisdom, interpreting the stars, writing calendars, studying geometry, and presiding over religious holidays.

They can influence the hearts and minds of others, their words compelling their companions to great deeds and filling their enemies with terror. They also have an affinity for time and fate, enabling them to predict the future.

Role: Communing with the gods, divining the future, and curing the ill are the primary tasks of a priestess. The priestess’s strength lies in influencing others, motivating them, advising them, rallying them, supporting them, and in some cases leading them.

Alignment: Varies by deity. A priestess’s alignment must be within one step of her deity’s, and it may not be neutral unless the deity’s is neutral.

Hit Die: d6.

Class Skills

The priestess’s class skills (and the key ability for each skill) are Appraise (Int), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Knowledge (all skills), Linguistics (Int), Perform (oratory) (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

A priestess who chooses Hate as one of her domains also has Intimidate (Cha) as a class skill. A priestess who chooses Trickery as one of her domains also has Bluff (Cha), Disguise (Cha), and Stealth (Dex) as class skills.

See Deity, Domains, and Domain Spells, below, for more information.

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the priestess.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Priestesses are skilled with the club, dagger, gastraphetes, manuballista, and quartertaff. Priestesses are not proficient with any type of armor or with shields. Priestesses consider it a point of pride to wield their deity’s favored weapon. A priestess whose deity’s favored weapon is a martial weapon and who chooses War as one of her domains receives the Martial Weapon Proficiency feat related to that weapon for free, as well as the Weapon Focus feat related to that weapon.

Aura (Ex)

A priestess of a chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity has a particularly powerful aura corresponding to the deity’s alignment (see the detect evil spell for details).

Mystic Skills (Ex)

Certain priestesses have access to some of the mystic’s skill unlocks. A priestess with Prophecy as one of her domains has the Prognostication mystic skill unlock. Depending on her religion, she may use horoscopy, cartomancy, or another form of divination. A priestess with Agriculture or Earth as one of her domains also has Dowsing as a mystic skill. A priestess with the Healing domain also has the Faith Healing mystic skill. A priestess with the Knowledge domain also has the Automatic Writing mystic skill.

Spellcasting

A priestess casts divine spells. A priestess may prepare and cast any spell on the priestess spell list, provided she can cast spells of that level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a priestess’s spell is 10 + the spell’s level + the priestess’s Wisdom modifier.

Each priestess must choose a time at which she must spend an hour each day in quiet contemplation or supplication to regain her daily allotment of spells. Time spent resting has no effect on whether a priestess can prepare spells.

In addition to her standard spells, a priestess gets one domain spell of each spell level, starting at 1st. When a priestess prepares a domain spell, it must come from one of her two domains.

Deity, Domains, and Domain Spells: Choose a deity for your priestess. The priest’s deity influences her alignment, what magic she can perform, her values, and how others see her. See Appendix III for a list of deities.

Choose two from among the deity’s domains for your priestess’s domains. You can only select an alignment domain (such as Good) for your priestess if her alignment matches that domain. If your priestess is not devoted to a particular deity, you still select two domains to represent her spiritual inclinations and abilities (but the restriction on alignment domains still applies).

Each domain gives your priestess access to a domain spell at each spell level, from 1st on up, as well as a granted power. Your priestess gets the granted powers of all the domains selected. With access to two domain spells at a given spell level, a priestess prepares one or the other each day. If a domain spell is not on the Priestess Spell List, a priestess can only prepare it in her domain slot.

Spontaneous Casting: Good priestesses (and neutral priestesses of good deities) can channel stored spell energy into healing spells that they haven’t prepared ahead of time. The priestess can “lose” a prepared spell in order to cast any cure spell of the same level or lower (a cure spell is any spell with “cure” in its name).

An evil priestess (or a neutral priestess of an evil deity), on the other hand, can’t convert prepared spells to cure spells but can convert them to inflict spells (an inflict spell is one with “inflict” in the title).

A priestess who is neither good nor evil and whose deity is neither good nor evil can convert spells either to cure spells or to inflict spells (player’s choice), depending on whether the priestess is more proficient at wielding positive or negative energy. Once the player makes this choice, it cannot be reversed. This choice also determines whether the neutral priestess turns or commands undead (see below).

Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells: A priestess can’t cast spells of an alignment opposed to her own or to her deity’s.

Channel Energy (Su)

Regardless of alignment, any priestess can release a wave of energy by channeling the power of her faith through her holy (or unholy) symbol.

This energy can be used to cause or heal damage, depending on the type of energy channeled and the creatures targeted.

A good priestess (or one who worships a good deity) channels positive energy and can choose to deal damage to undead creatures or to heal living creatures. An evil priestess (or one who worships an evil deity) channels negative energy and can choose to deal damage to living creatures or to heal undead creatures. A neutral priestess who worships a neutral deity (or one who is not devoted to a particular deity) must choose whether she channels positive or negative energy. Once this choice is made, it cannot be reversed. This decision also determines whether the priestess casts spontaneous cure or inflict spells (see spontaneous casting).

Channeling energy causes a burst that affects all creatures of one type (either undead or living) in a 30-foot radius centered on the priestess. The amount of damage dealt or healed is equal to 1d6 points of damage plus 1d6 points of damage for every two priestess levels beyond 1st (2d6 at 3rd, 3d6 at 5th, and so on). Creatures that take damage from channeled energy receive a Will save to halve the damage. The DC of this save is equal to 10 + 1/2 the priestess’s level + the priestess’s Charisma modifier. Creatures healed by channeled energy cannot exceed their maximum hit point total—all excess healing is lost. A priestess may channel energy a number of times per day equal to 5 + her Charisma modifier. This is a standard action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity. A priestess can choose whether or not to include herself in this effect. A priestess must be able to present her holy symbol to use this ability.

Divine Grace (Su)

A priestess adds her Charisma modifier (if positive) as a bonus to all saving throws.

Bonus Languages: A priestess’s list of bonus languages includes Celestial, Abyssal, and Infernal, in addition to the bonus languages available to the character because of her homeland (see Languages).

Preaching: A priestess can use the Perform (oratory) skill to create magical effects on those around her, including herself if desired. She can use this ability to preach sermons and prayers for a number of rounds per day equal to 4 + her Charisma modifier. At each level after 1st a priestess can preach for 2 additional rounds per day. Each round, the priestess can produce any one of the types of prayers or sermons that she has mastered, as indicated by her level.

Preaching is a standard action to begin, but it can be maintained each round thereafter as a free action.

Changing a sermon or prayer from one effect to another requires the priestess to stop the previous preaching and start a new one as a standard action. Preaching cannot be disrupted, but it ends immediately if the priestess is killed, paralyzed, stunned, knocked unconscious, or otherwise prevented from taking a free action to maintain it each round. A priestess cannot have more than one sermon or prayer in effect at one time.

At 7th level, a priestess can start preaching as a move action instead of a standard action.

All sermons and prayers have audible components and targets must be able to hear the priestess for the preaching to have any effect. Some sermons and prayers are also language dependent (as noted in the description). A deaf priestess has a 20% chance to fail when attempting to use preaching. If she fails this check, the attempt still counts against her daily limit. Deaf creatures are immune to preaching.

If a sermon or prayer has a visual component, the targets must have line of sight to the priestess for the preaching to have any effect. A blind priest has a 50% chance to fail when attempting to use a sermon or prayer with a visual component. If she fails this check, the attempt still counts against her daily limit. Blind creatures are immune to preaching with visual components.

Counterspeech (Su)

At 1st level, a priestess learns to counter magic effects that depend on sound (but not spells that have verbal components). Each round of the counterspeech she makes a Perform (oratory) skill check. Any creature within 30 feet of the priestess (including the priestess herself) that is affected by a sonic or language-dependent magical attack may use the priestess’s Perform check result in place of its saving throw if, after the saving throw is rolled, the Perform check result proves to be higher. If a creature within range of the counterspeech is already under the effect of a noninstantaneous sonic or language-dependent magical attack, it gains another saving throw against the effect each round it hears the counterspeech, but it must use the priestess’s Perform skill check result for the save.

Counterspeech does not work on effects that don’t allow saves. Counterspeech relies on audible components.

Distraction (Su)

At 1st level, a priestess can use her performance to counter magic effects that depend on sight. Each round of the distraction, she makes a Perform (oratory) skill check. Any creature within 30 feet of the priestess (including the priestess herself) that is affected by an illusion (pattern) or illusion (figment) magical attack may use the priestess’s Perform check result in place of its saving throw if, after the saving throw is rolled, the Perform skill check proves to be higher. If a creature within range of the distraction is already under the effect of a noninstantaneous illusion (pattern) or illusion (figment) magical attack, it gains another saving throw against the effect each round it sees the distraction, but it must use the priestess’s Perform skill check result for the save.

Distraction does not work on effects that don’t allow saves. Distraction relies on visual components.

Fascinate (Su)

At 1st level, a priestess can use her preaching to cause one or more creatures to become fascinated with her. Each creature to be fascinated must be within 90 feet, able to see and hear the priestess, and capable of paying attention to her. The priestess must also be able to see the creatures affected. The distraction of a nearby combat or other dangers prevents this ability from working. For every three levels the priestess has attained beyond 1st, she can target one additional creature with this ability.

Each creature within range receives a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 the priestess’s level + the priest’s Cha modifier) to negate the effect. If a creature’s saving throw succeeds, the priestess cannot attempt to fascinate that creature again for 24 hours. If its saving throw fails, the creature sits quietly and observes the performance for as long as the priestess continues to maintain it. While fascinated, a target takes a –4 penalty on all skill checks made as reactions, such as Perception checks. Any potential threat to the target allows the target to make a new saving throw against the effect. Any obvious threat, such as someone drawing a weapon, casting a spell, or aiming a weapon at the target, automatically breaks the effect. Fascinate is an enchantment (compulsion), mind-affecting ability. Fascinate relies on audible and visual components in order to function.

Inspire Courage (Su)

A 1st level priestess can use her performance to inspire courage in her allies (including herself), bolstering them against fear and improving their combat abilities. To be affected, an ally must be able to perceive the priestess’s performance. An affected ally receives a +1 morale bonus on saving throws against charm and fear effects and a +1 competence bonus on attack and weapon damage rolls. At 5th level, this bonus increases by +1. Inspire courage is a mind-affecting ability. Inspire courage has audible components.

Inspire Competence (Su)

A priestess of 3rd level or higher can use her performance to help an ally succeed at a task. That ally must be within 30 feet and be able to hear the priestess. The ally gets a +2 competence bonus on skill checks with a particular skill as long as she continues to hear the priestess’s performance. This bonus increases by +1 at 7th.

Certain uses of this ability are infeasible, such as Stealth, and may be disallowed at the GM’s discretion.

A priestess can’t inspire competence in herself.

Inspire competence relies on audible components.

Suggestion (Sp)

A priestess of 6th level or higher can use her performance to make a suggestion (as per the spell) to a creature she has already fascinated (see above). Using this ability does not disrupt the fascinate effect, but it does require a standard action to activate (in addition to the free action to continue the fascinate effect). A priestess can use this ability more than once against an individual creature during an individual performance. Suggestion is an enchantment (compulsion), mind-affecting, language-dependent ability that relies on audible components.

Inspire Greatness (Su)

A priestess of 9th level or higher can use her preaching to inspire greatness in herself or a single willing ally within 30 feet, granting extra fighting capability. To inspire greatness, the target must be able to see and hear the priestess. A creature inspired with greatness gains 2 bonus Hit Dice (d10s), the commensurate number of temporary hit points (apply the target’s Constitution modifier, if any, to these bonus Hit Dice), a +2 competence bonus on attack rolls, and a +1 competence bonus on Fortitude saves. The bonus Hit Dice count as regular Hit Dice for determining the effect of spells that are Hit Dice dependent. Inspire greatness is a mind-affecting ability and it relies on audible and visual components.

Sermon of Doom (Su)

A priestess of 8th level or higher can use his preaching to foster a sense of growing dread in his enemies, causing them to become shaken. To be affected, an enemy must be within 30 feet and able to see and hear the priestess’s preaching. The effect persists for as long as the enemy is within 30 feet and the priestess continues her performance. This performance cannot cause a creature to become frightened or panicked, even if the targets are already shaken from another effect.

Sermon of doom is a mind-affecting fear effect, and it relies on audible and visual components.

Well-Versed (Ex)

At 2nd level, the priestess becomes resistant to bardic performances, preaching, and to sonic effects in general. The priestess gains a +4 bonus on saving throws made against bardic performance, preaching, sonic, and language-dependent effects.

Cohort (Ex)

Upon reaching 4th level, priestesses gain a special cohort, as determined by the Leadership feat. The priestess has a reputation of having a special power in the eyes of this cohort (+1 Leadership bonus).

This cohort is always of the same alignment as the priestess. Any followers indicated by the priestess’s Leadership score also accompany this cohort.

Lore Master (Ex)

At 5th level, the priestess becomes a master of lore and can take 10 on any Knowledge skill check that she has ranks in. A priestess can choose not to take 10 and can instead roll normally. In addition, once per day, the priestess can take 20 on any Knowledge skill check as a standard action. She can use this ability one additional time per day at 10th level.

Sycophant (Ex)

At 8th level, the priestess acquires a dedicated follower who faithfully obeys her commands.

The level and class of this sycophant are determined with the rules regarding cohorts in the Leadership feat, except that the priestess has a reputation of having a special power in the eyes of the sycophant (+1 Leadership bonus). The sycophant is also always of the same alignment as the priestess. If the priestess has caused the death of a previous sycophant or cohort, it does not negatively affect her Leadership score when attracting a sycophant. Any followers indicated by the priestess’s Leadership score also accompany this sycophant.

Ex-Priestesses

A priestess who egregiously violates the code of conduct expected by her god (acting in ways that oppose the god’s alignment or purposes) loses all class features and cannot gain levels as a priestess of that god until she atones.

Priestess Spell List

4th-Level Priestess Spells–air walk, chaos hammer, Control Water, Cure Critical Wounds, Death Ward, Dimensional Anchor, Discern Lies, Dismissal, Divination, Divine Power, Freedom of Movement, Giant Vermin, Holy Smite, Imbue with Spell Ability, Inflict Critical Wounds, Magic Weapon, Greater, Neutralize Poison, Order’s Wrath, Planar Ally, Lesser, Poison, Repel Vermin, Restoration, Sending, Spell Immunity, Summon Monster IV, Tongues, Unholy Blight
